headline: Bank of Canada Holds at 2.25% as May CPI Snapshots +2.8% and Housing Starts Climb to 279,317 SAAR
executive_summary:
The Bank of Canada held its overnight rate at 2.25% on June 10, a second consecutive hold delivered alongside the latest Monetary Policy Report — the decision leaves 1,862 active rate-sensitive construction projects ($284.3B) financing against a Government of Canada curve whose 5-year benchmark sits at 3.04%, the mortgage-renewal anchor for residential and commercial borrowers.1 The next scheduled decision is July 9, sequenced one week after US June payrolls.2

Headline CPI registered +2.8% year-over-year on the latest snapshot, up 0.4 percentage points, with the formal May print scheduled for June 17 — core-trim and core-median both sit at 2.0%, while April component detail recorded energy +28.6% y/y, food +3.8% y/y, and shelter +1.8% y/y.5 Average hourly wage fell 1.4% month-over-month to $37.24 in May, set against the +2.8% headline pace.4

Monthly real GDP declined 0.1% in March 2026, with the April GDP-by-industry release scheduled for June 24 — mining, quarrying and oil-and-gas extraction GDP fell 2.1% month-over-month and manufacturing GDP ran 2.5% below year-ago levels, even as April manufacturing sales rose 4.2% m/m to $77,052.9M.36 The database tracks 346 active manufacturing projects ($70.0B) and 642 mining/oil-and-gas projects ($263.1B) against those readings.

Unemployment held at 6.6% in May while housing starts rose to 279,317 SAAR, up 6.9% from the April pace of 261,377 — the employment rate stood at 60.7% and participation at 65.0%, with accommodation and food employment up 4.3% m/m against retail down 1.8% m/m.4 April residential building permits fell 5.5% m/m and non-residential permits fell 10.5% m/m, even as starts advanced; the database tracks 272 active residential projects ($41.6B).817

WTI crude settled at $80.58/bbl, down 11.7% on the week and 23.6% over the month, framing the energy-export picture into next week's data calendar — the price remains above the $74–76 breakeven cluster the cross-reference engine cites for 91 active oil-and-gas projects ($63.2B), and April energy exports rose 9.7% m/m to $19.88B.14 The June 17 CPI print and FOMC decision, the June 24 April GDP release, and the July 9 Bank of Canada decision sequence the indicators that will reset this picture.521

national.analysis:
Monthly real GDP contracted 0.1% in March 2026, down 0.2 percentage points from the +0.1% February pace, according to Statistics Canada — the April GDP-by-industry release is scheduled for June 24 and will carry sectoral detail across all 20 NAICS industries.3 The March decline was led by goods-producing industries: mining, quarrying and oil-and-gas extraction fell 2.1% month-over-month, and on a year-over-year basis manufacturing ran 2.5% below 2025 levels while mining sat 1.5% lower and construction 1.5% lower.

Industry GDP diverged sharply across services in the March reference month — finance and insurance rose 3.6% y/y, information and cultural industries 3.2% y/y, and transportation and warehousing 3.1% y/y, against management of companies and enterprises at -22.7% y/y, a small, volatile aggregate.3 Manufacturing told a two-speed story: GDP -2.5% y/y while April manufacturing sales rose 4.2% m/m to $77,052.9M and wholesale sales rose 2.8% m/m to $138,830.0M.67 The database tracks 346 active manufacturing projects ($70.0B).

The labour market held its level in May, with unemployment at 6.6% and the employment rate at 60.7% — participation stood at 65.0% and average hourly wage fell 1.4% m/m to $37.24.49 By industry, accommodation and food employment rose 4.3% m/m while retail employment fell 1.8% m/m. The next Labour Force Survey, covering June, is scheduled for July 3.

The Bank of Canada held the overnight rate at 2.25% on June 10, its second consecutive hold — the decision was paired with the Monetary Policy Report and leaves the 5-year Government of Canada benchmark at 3.04% as the mortgage-renewal anchor for 1,862 active rate-sensitive construction projects ($284.3B).1 Headline CPI registered +2.8% y/y on the latest snapshot with the formal May print due June 17; core-trim and core-median both held at 2.0%.5

Housing starts rose to 279,317 SAAR in May, up 6.9% from the April pace of 261,377, even as April building permits declined — residential permits fell 5.5% m/m and non-residential permits fell 10.5% m/m, and the new housing price index eased 0.4% m/m to 121.1 in April.81017 The database tracks 272 active residential projects ($41.6B). On trade, April merchandise exports reached $66.3B, with energy exports up 9.7% m/m to $19.88B; WTI crude settled at $80.58/bbl, down 11.7% on the week and 23.6% over the month, above the $74–76 breakeven cluster cited for 91 active oil-and-gas projects ($63.2B).14 Capital expenditure intentions for 2026 stand at $401,203M, up 3.7% y/y.11

Across the broader sector map, services GDP held up against goods-producing weakness in the March reference month — retail trade GDP rose 0.8% y/y and wholesale trade 1.0% y/y, real estate, rental and leasing 1.8% y/y, and public administration 1.1% y/y, against arts, entertainment and recreation up 3.5% y/y.3 Household disposable income reached $1,811,968M in Q1 2026, up 0.6% q/q, while the savings rate eased to 3.5% from 3.7%.12 The database tracks 6,485 active projects valued at $1,620.8B, with 135 newly recorded this week, spanning the rate-sensitive construction, residential, and energy pipelines that finance against the indicators above.

consumer_pulse:
Cost-of-living pressure framed the consumer picture, with headline CPI at +2.8% y/y while average hourly wage fell 1.4% m/m to $37.24 in May — April component detail recorded food +3.8% y/y and shelter +1.8% y/y, and the new housing price index eased 0.4% m/m to 121.1, its first negative print after flat-to-rising months.5910 The 5-year Government of Canada yield at 3.04% sets the mortgage-renewal anchor.

Energy costs eased over the month as WTI crude fell to $80.58/bbl from $96.60 a month earlier, lowering a gasoline-relevant input — by contrast, April energy CPI ran 28.6% above year-ago levels.514 The household savings rate stood at 3.5% in Q1 2026, down 0.2 percentage points from 3.7%, with disposable income up 0.6% q/q; the 2-year Government of Canada yield at 2.76%, down 22 bps y/y, lowers the GIC anchor.12

Labour and fiscal signals rounded out the picture across the hard data stack — accommodation and food employment rose 4.3% m/m against retail down 1.8% m/m, while the federal Spring Economic Update 2026 committed $51B in infrastructure, a sovereign fund, and a CCUS-EOR tax-credit expansion.418 Housing starts rose to 279,317 SAAR in May, up 6.9% from the April pace, while the new housing price index eased 0.4% m/m to 121.1.1017 A CUSMA review remains open alongside tariff threats referenced in the prior edition.20

global.analysis: The Federal Reserve held its funds target at 3.50–3.75% from the April 29 decision and meets June 16–17 with an updated Summary of Economic Projections, the first decision under Chair Kevin Warsh — the Philadelphia Fed Survey of Professional Forecasters records Q1 2026 GDP at +2.6% and full-year growth at +2.5%, with core CPI at +2.6% y/y on the March reference.212223 The Fed–BoC differential sits near +125 bps against the BoC at 2.25%, sustaining CAD/USD at 0.7161, down 2.63% y/y. CUSMA renegotiation and tariff threats overhang 346 active Canadian manufacturing projects ($70.0B).

China's May NBS Manufacturing PMI printed at the 50.0 expansion threshold, down 0.3 points on the month, with the new-orders sub-index at 49.9 in contraction — the composite PMI rose 0.4 points to 50.5, with high-tech manufacturing at 52.9 and equipment manufacturing at 52.1, while the People's Bank of China held the 1-year loan prime rate at the May 20 fixing.25 Copper at $6.51/lb, up 35.59% y/y, and the iron-ore proxy up 16.10% y/y frame sustained industrial demand against 551 active Canadian mining projects ($199.9B). USD/CNY stands at 6.76, down 6.02% y/y.

The European Central Bank raised its deposit facility 25 bps to 2.25% effective June 17, its first hike in three years — the main refinancing rate moved to 2.40% and the marginal lending rate to 2.65%, against HICP running +3.2% y/y on the April reference, the highest since 2023, with core at +2.5%.2627 Q1 2026 GDP contracted 0.2%, while the Survey of Professional Forecasters carries full-year growth at +0.9%. The hike narrows the ECB–BoC deposit differential to zero, with both policy rates at 2.25%; EUR/USD stands at 1.16.

global.analysis: The Bank of England held Bank Rate at 3.75%, set April 30 by an 8–1 vote with one member voting to hike, and its June 18 MPC meeting is market-priced for a hold — the BoE central projection places CPI at 3.1% in Q2 2026, rising to 3.3% in Q3 before easing.28 The UK–Canada policy-rate differential stands at +150 bps, and GBP/USD trades at 1.3450, down 1.31% y/y. The United Kingdom is a destination for Canadian gold, which trades at $4,353/oz, up 31.07% y/y, alongside uranium and select agricultural exports.
